Q: How to fix zsh: corrupt history file /home/mis/.zsh_history (Linux) A:

Just delete it with rm ~/.zsh_history, then kill all your open terminals, e.g. pkill kitty

The file auto-regenerates (I think if any instance of zsh is open is the condition for it to do so).

When I used these commands I actually used sudo rm ~/.zsh_history but I don't think the sudo is necessary, I did it because I was confused by the auto-regeneration.

Q: c++ multiple processes writing to the same file - Interprocess mutex? A:

In the scenario where you are communicating between multiple processes, the C++ standard library does not say anything about processes. It does not specify that its mutexes can be shared between different processes.

However, POSIX (and Linux) have a mutex attribute, PTHREAD_PROCESS_SHARED, which enables threads in different processes to use the same pthread_mutex_t in shared memory, such as from shmat() or mmap(). On Windows, a thread in another process can share a named mutex object using OpenMutex() or an unnamed mutex by duplicating its handle with DuplicateHandle()..
